## 1. Goal

Make Compare answer one question first: which scheduler did best on these jobs. Verdict sentence first, then the metric table, timelines, exact optimum and charts.

## 2. Background

**Design authority:** `docs/design/APPLE_DESIGN.md` (added by K-43). Direction "soft sheets": flat solid colours, hairline borders, one whisper shadow, translucent top bar and dock (`backdrop-filter`, solid fallback under `prefers-reduced-transparency` and `prefers-contrast: more`), no gradients except the scroll-edge fade, no glows, neon, purple, emoji icons or monospace fonts. System sans-serif only; numbers use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

**Palette (final):** light canvas `#F2F3F1`, surface `#FFFFFF`, text `#1B1F1D`, muted `#5B625E`, border `#CFD3D0`, accent teal `#0B5E6B`, red `#B42318`, amber `#8A4B00`, green `#1D7A34`, chart gray `#8A918D`. Dark: canvas `#121513`, surface `#1B1F1D`, text `#ECEFED`, muted `#A3ABA6`, border `#343A37`, accent `#5FB6C4`, red `#F0877C`, amber `#E0A24A`, green `#6FCB87`, chart gray `#8A918D`. Chart gray is for chart marks and rules only, never text.

**Rules that do not change (CLAUDE.md rule 7, PRD §7 and §8):** classic scripts on `window.APRM`, no ES modules, no `fetch`, no framework, no build step; works from `file://` offline; `textContent` only for user, file, URL and engine text; loading, empty and error states on every view; colours as CSS variables with light and dark values; Chart.js only in Compare, pinned with SRI, with a table fallback. Nothing here touches `core/`, `wasm/` or PRD §5, and every number shown must equal the engine JSON.

**Tone:** short plain sentences, sentence case, talk to the user. Plain words first, technical term beside them ("Shortest job first (SJF)"). Engine sentences (why log, validation errors) are shown verbatim; the UI may add a plain lead-in but never rewrites them. "Show details" (K-43) reveals the full technical view: exact numbers, raw aged keys, heap order, log kinds.

## 3. Scope

**In scope:**

- Scheduler picker with plain names and the technical term beside them
- Verdict sentence built from the engine metrics (best makespan, gap to others)
- Metric table with the best value marked by the word "Best" as well as colour; a dash means no value
- Exact best order and gap for 9 jobs or fewer; stacked timelines using the K-45 canvas style
- Charts in the new palette (chart gray for neutral marks) with the table fallback

**Out of scope:**

- Run page
- Any change to Chart.js version or SRI (unchanged)

## 5. Specification

The verdict is computed only from metric values returned by the engine (min makespan, ties named). Ties are listed, not hidden. All numbers equal the console program for the same case.

## 6. Step-by-step tasks

1. Write verdict and number tests first
2. Restyle picker, table and timelines
3. Restyle charts and keep the fallback
4. Screenshots light and dark before and after

## 7. Tests to write

| Test name | What it checks | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| verdict | Verdict names the best scheduler and the gap; ties named | Matches metrics |
| compare-numbers | Table equals the console program for the same case | Equal |
| best-mark | Best marked by text and colour | Pass |
| chart-fallback | Without Chart.js the table fallback shows | Pass |

## 8. Acceptance criteria (Done when)

- [ ] Verdict sentence first, then table, timelines, exact optimum and charts
- [ ] Best marked by text, not colour alone
- [ ] Numbers equal the console program
- [ ] node tests/web/*.mjs green; file:// offline; screenshots in the PR

## 9. How to verify

`node tests/web/*.mjs`; compare all six schedulers on each preset and check against `build/aprm`.

## 10. Viva notes

Compare runs one engine per scheduler on the same jobs. Examiner question: "How do you know the optimum is exact?" The exact solver is exhaustive up to 9 jobs.

## 11. Pitfalls

- Verdict claiming more than the numbers show
- Colour-only highlighting
